card: This draft PR modifies socket read behavior to artificially return data in tiny chunks or single bytes to stress-test networking code against unexpected TCP segmentation. It is designed to identify code paths across the node that make fragile assumptions about socket buffer chunking. The author explicitly states this is a temporary reproducer run not intended for merging and will be closed after test runs complete.
evidence: Author description: 'All networking code using sockets must not make assumption about the chunking of the incoming/outgoing data, and should be resilient against any chunking.'
Author description: 'WARNING: NOT INTENDED FOR MERGING!... This PR will be closed once the test runs complete, and kept for reference (some tests are expected to fail).'
problem: TCP and IP provide a stream abstraction without message boundary guarantees, but networking code can accidentally rely on sender chunking matching receiver chunking. Currently, developers lack a stress-testing mechanism to uncover code paths that make invalid assumptions about incoming chunk sizes.

risk.why: Forcing single-byte or tiny chunk socket receives in production code would drastically degrade network throughput and CPU performance for all peer communications.

scope_notes: This PR is explicitly marked DONTMERGE and draft; it is intended solely as an automated test harness to observe CI failures under fragmented socket reads.
summary: Modifies socket receive operations to intentionally read data in small chunks or single bytes rather than reading all available buffer data at once. It also updates `sock_tests` to accommodate chunked receives. The pull request is an explicit test-only reproducer marked not for merging, used to trigger CI and observe how networking code handles fragmented input.
